packages.name: event-stream
evidence: SOURCE: event-stream@3.3.6 was the poisoned release, published 2018-09-09.
The attacker transferred ownership of event-stream from its original maintainer and published 3.3.6 with flatmap-stream@0.1.1 added as a direct dependency.
3.3.6 was unpublished from npm after the incident and is no longer downloadable.
Verified: https://blog.npmjs.org/post/180565383195/details-about-the-event-stream-incident

packages.name: flatmap-stream
evidence: PAYLOAD: flatmap-stream@0.1.1 contained an AES-256 encrypted malicious payload.
The payload decrypted itself only when the consuming project's package.json description matched a specific value (targeting Copay wallet: 'A Secure Bitcoin Wallet').
0.1.1 was unpublished from npm after the incident. Only 0.0.1-security (a safety stub) remains.
Verified: https://blog.npmjs.org/post/180565383195/details-about-the-event-stream-incident

packages.name: ps-tree
evidence: L1: ps-tree@1.1.0 is present in the event-stream dependency graph as a consumer (depends on event-stream).
L2: range '~3.3.0' ADMITS event-stream@3.3.6 (the build that pulled in flatmap-stream@0.1.1).
L3 CHAIN WALK: REACHABLE
HOP ps-tree@1.1.0 -> event-stream: UNCONDITIONAL — package/index.js: line 4: `es    = require('event-stream');` (appears before first control-flow at line 97)

HOP event-stream@3.3.6 -> flatmap-stream: DOCUMENTED UNCONDITIONAL — npm postmortem confirms event-stream@3.3.6 added require('flatmap-stream') unconditionally to its index.js. Source: https://blog.npmjs.org/post/180565383195/details-about-the-event-stream-incident

packages.name: live-server
evidence: L1: live-server@1.2.0 is present in the event-stream dependency graph as a consumer (depends on event-stream).

L2: range 'latest' ADMITS event-stream@3.3.6 — at incident time (Oct 2018) 'latest' resolved to the poisoned 3.3.6 release. Maintainer pinned to '3.3.4' in v1.2.1 published 2018-11-26 (post-incident).
L3 CHAIN WALK: REACHABLE
HOP live-server@1.2.0 -> event-stream: UNCONDITIONAL — package/index.js: line 12: `es = require("event-stream"),` (appears before first control-flow at line 25)

HOP event-stream@3.3.6 -> flatmap-stream: DOCUMENTED UNCONDITIONAL — npm postmortem confirms event-stream@3.3.6 added require('flatmap-stream') unconditionally to its index.js. Source: https://blog.npmjs.org/post/180565383195/details-about-the-event-stream-incident

packages.name: nodemon
evidence: L1: nodemon@1.12.5 is present in the event-stream dependency graph as a consumer (depends on event-stream).
L2: N/A — nodemon has no direct event-stream dependency. It resolves event-stream transitively via ps-tree@^1.1.0, which declares event-stream ~3.3.0 (ADMITS 3.3.6).

L3: Not reachable — transitive consumer does not directly require event-stream. The malicious code would only execute if this package's dependencies are installed and event-stream is loaded by one of them (ps-tree here). This package itself does not trigger the chain.

historical_reference.documented_impact: For a typical supply-chain injection, our reachability funnel correctly flags every real consumer as exposed. What it cannot detect — and we say so rather than hide it — is a runtime-conditional targeted payload like event-stream's, which decrypted itself only for one specific victim using data our static analysis never executes. That class of attack requires dynamic or behavioral analysis: a distinct, harder problem we've scoped as future work, not something this tool claims to solve.
